title: Grade 2 Science — Thu, May 21
description: Plants Around Us — Day 4 of 5: How plants reproduce and grow
subject: science

questions.question: What is germination?
options: A seed starting to grow into a new plant
questions.explanation: Germination is when a seed begins to sprout and grow into a new plant. It needs water, warmth, and soil.

questions.question: Which comes first when a seed grows?
questions.explanation: The first thing to come out of a germinating seed is the tiny root (radicle). It grows downward into the soil.

questions.question: How do coconut seeds travel to new places?
questions.explanation: Coconuts float in water — ocean currents carry them to new shores. This is seed dispersal by water.

questions.question: Dandelion seeds have fluffy white tufts. How do they travel?
questions.explanation: Dandelion seeds have fluffy parachutes that are carried by the wind to new places. This is wind dispersal.

questions.question: Some fruits have hooks that stick to animal fur. What kind of dispersal is this?
questions.explanation: Fruits with hooks stick to animal fur or human clothes and get carried to new places. This is animal dispersal.

questions.question: What does a seed need to germinate?
questions.explanation: A seed needs water (to soften the seed coat), warmth, and air (oxygen) to germinate. Sunlight is not needed for germination.

questions.question: After the seed germinates, what happens next?
questions.explanation: After germination, a tiny plant called a seedling grows. It has a small root, stem, and the first tiny leaves.

questions.question: Can plants grow from other parts besides seeds?
options: Yes — from stems, leaves, or roots too
questions.explanation: Many plants grow from stem cuttings (rose, money plant), leaves (jade plant), or roots. Farmers use this to grow plants faster.

questions.question: The potato plant grows new plants from:
questions.explanation: Potatoes have 'eyes' (buds) on their surface. A piece of potato with an eye can grow into a new plant.

questions.question: Why is seed dispersal important?
options: It spreads plants to new places so they don't crowd each other
questions.explanation: Seed dispersal helps plants spread to new areas. If all seeds fell in one place, they would compete for water, light, and nutrients.

questions.question: Which of these plants grows from a cutting (stem)?
questions.explanation: Money plant grows easily from stem cuttings placed in water or soil. Many ornamental plants are grown this way.

questions.question: A new plant grown from a seed will look exactly like:
questions.explanation: Seeds carry the genetic information of the parent plant. A mango seed grows into a mango tree.

questions.question: What do we call the first leaves of a germinating seed?
questions.explanation: The first leaves inside a seed are called seed leaves or cotyledons. They provide food to the seedling until it can make its own.

questions.question: A mango tree takes many years to grow. A mustard plant grows in:
questions.explanation: Mustard (sarson) is a fast-growing plant that completes its life cycle in a few weeks. Different plants grow at different speeds.

questions.question: Roots always grow:
questions.explanation: Roots always grow downward (toward gravity) into the soil. Stems grow upward toward light. This is called tropism.
